Sitting atop the kidneys, this pair of endocrine glands produces hormones including adrenaline, aldosterone, and cortisol. What organ is it?
Adrenal gland (also known as suprarenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including adrenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.

Sitting at the milder end of a spectrum of diminished motivation — less severe than abulia and far short of akinetic mutism — this is a state marked by an absence of feeling, interest, or concern. What is it?
Apathy is a lack of feeling, emotion, interest, and/or concern about something.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.

David Attenborough called this English particle physicist the natural successor for the BBC's scientific programming, thanks to shows like The Infinite Monkey Cage and his Wonders of... series — who is he?
Brian Cox (physicist) (born 3 March 1968) is an English physicist and musician.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
A scale insect native to tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas that lives on prickly-pear cacti, this parasite is the source of the natural dye carmine — which insect?
Cochineal (-eel, US also, -eel; Dactylopius coccus) is a scale insect in the suborder Sternorrhyncha, from which the natural dye carmine is derived.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.
When insulin runs short, the body burns fat into acidic ketones, causing deep gasping breaths and fruity-smelling breath in this potentially life-threatening emergency — what is it?
Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) is a potentially life-threatening acute complication of diabetes mellitus.
Born in Dublin in 1869 into an old Anglo-Irish scientific family, she's considered the very first woman to work as a medical physicist — who was she?
Edith Anne Stoney (6 January 1869 - 25 June 1938) was an Irish physicist.

This Austrian physicist devised a foundational equation for calculating a quantum system's wave function and coined the term 'quantum entanglement,' sharing the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Paul Dirac — who is he?
Erwin Schrödinger (12 August 1887 - 4 January 1961), sometimes written as Schroedinger or Schrodinger, was an Austrian theoretical physicist who developed fundamental results in quantum theory.
This body part is a prominent, usually flexible digit found on the forelimbs of most four-limbed vertebrates — on the hind limbs, the equivalent shorter digits are instead called toes. What is it?
Finger is a prominent digit on the forelimbs of most tetrapod vertebrate animals, especially those with prehensile extremities (i.e.
Testimony at Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán's 2018 trial revealed suitcases stuffed with $3 million in bribes paid to this former Mexican security chief — who is he?
Genaro García Luna (born 10 July 1968) is a Mexican former government official and convicted drug trafficker.
Designed in the late 1950s as a replacement for the piston-engined E-1 Tracer, this twin-turboprop U.S. Navy aircraft provides carrier-based early warning radar coverage. Name the aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.

Fox-sized and found on every continent but Australia and Antarctica, these primitive ornithischian dinosaurs are known for odd teeth — canine-like tusks plus cheek teeth built for chewing. What's this family?
Heterodontosauridae is a family of ornithischian dinosaurs that were likely among the most basal (primitive) members of the group.
This birth defect, found in roughly one in every 250 newborn boys, involves an opening that fails to form in its typical location — what condition is this?

Hypospadias is a common malformation in fetal development, most commonly noticed in penises, in which the urethra does not open from its usual location on the head of the penis, or the middle of the vulva.
Serving as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician played a central role in creating the European single market and laying groundwork for the euro — who is he?
Jacques Delors (20 July 1925 - 27 December 2023) was a French politician who served as president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995.
Named after a 19th-century English physicist, this SI unit of energy equals the work done when a one-newton force moves an object one metre in the direction of that force — name the unit?
Joule (JOOL, or JOWL; symbol: J) is the unit of energy in the International System of Units (SI).
Which aromatic Mediterranean evergreen tree, prominent in classical Greco-Roman culture and used to season food, can grow up to 20 meters tall with smooth, glossy leaves?
Laurus nobilis is an aromatic evergreen tree or large shrub with green, glabrous (smooth) leaves.
Because its large profile and low operating altitude make it an easy target, this heavily armed gunship variant of the C-130 Hercules usually flies missions at night. What aircraft is it?
Lockheed AC-130 is a heavily armed, long-endurance, ground-attack variant of the C-130 Hercules transport, fixed-wing aircraft.

One of the most colorful mammals alive, this west-central African monkey wears red and blue on both its face and its rump, with the brightest males being the biggest — long mistaken for a baboon, what is it?
Mandrill (Mandrillus sphinx) is a large Old World monkey native to west central Africa.
Discovered in 1893 and existing as two enantiomers, this CNS stimulant is best known in its hydrochloride salt form as 'crystal meth' — what is it?

Methamphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is primarily used as a recreational or performance-enhancing drug and less commonly as a second-line treatment for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).
Their name means "little fly" in Spanish, and biologists class them as micropredators — all sip flower nectar, but the females of many species also drink blood. What are they?
Mosquito are a family of small flies consisting of 3,600 species.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).
Fossils of these arachnids in 400-million-year-old Scottish rock look startlingly modern — colloquially they're called harvestmen or daddy long legs. What order is this?
Opiliones (formerly Phalangida) are an order of arachnids, colloquially known as harvestmen, harvesters, daddy long legs, or granddaddy long legs.

One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory — the study of when order must inevitably appear — and cracked countless open problems across number theory and combinatorics; who was he?
Paul Erdős (26 March 1913 - 20 September 1996) was a Hungarian mathematician known as one of the most prolific mathematicians and producers of mathematical conjectures of the 20th century.

Derived from phosphoric acid by removing one to three protons, this anion or salt takes forms like dihydrogen and hydrogen variants and gives its name to fertilizers and various esters — name the ion?
Phosphate is an anion, salt, functional group or ester derived from a phosphoric acid.

Attacks of this condition — abdominal pain, vomiting, and confusion lasting days to weeks — stem from a buildup of porphyrins and can be triggered by stress, smoking, or certain medications. What is it?
Porphyria (or) is a group of disorders in which substances called porphyrins build up in the body, adversely affecting the skin or nervous system.
This kidney inflammation, most often caused by E. coli infection, typically causes fever and tenderness along the side of the body — what is it?
Pyelonephritis is inflammation of the kidney, typically due to a bacterial infection.
Made up of a large and small subunit built from RNA and proteins, this molecular machine found in every living cell translates messenger RNA into chains of amino acids — what is it?
Ribosome is a ribonucleoprotein particle found in all cells, both prokaryotic and eukaryotic, responsible for the synthesis of proteins.
Having coded his first game in high school and studied computer science in Tokyo, this man went on to lead Nintendo by championing fun over raw horsepower — who is he?
Satoru Iwata (December 6, 1959 - July 11, 2015) was a Japanese businessman, video game programmer and producer.

Developed by the Chukchi people in the Russian Far East for pulling sleds and companionship, this medium-sized Spitz-family dog breed is smaller than the similar-looking Alaskan Malamute — name the breed?
Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Turkish businesswoman served as one of her father's chief advisers back in 2013, when he held the office of prime minister and later became Turkey's president — who is she?
Sümeyye Erdoğan (ne Erdoan; born 22 August 1985) is a Turkish businesswoman and the daughter of President Recep Tayyip Erdoan.
What culinary herb — the dried aerial parts of plants in the mint family, native to the Mediterranean — is most commonly cultivated in its 'vulgaris' species from Southeast Europe?
Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria and contracted orally, this disease presents with gradual fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, rose-colored skin spots. What is it?
Typhoid fever is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.
Named after the Scottish engineer who improved the Newcomen steam engine in 1776, this SI unit of power equals one joule per second — what is it?
Watt (symbol: W) is the unit of power or radiant flux in the International System of Units (SI), equal to 1 joule per second or 1 kgm2s3.

Released from prison in June 2025 to resume leading Turkey's nationalist Victory Party, this politician previously served as deputy leader of the far-right Nationalist Movement Party in the mid-2010s — who is he?
Ümit Özdağ (born 3 March 1961) is a Turkish politician who returned to his position as the current leader of the Victory Party after being released from prison on 17 June 2025.
Nicknamed for the stripes on its legs and body, this day-biting mosquito native to Southeast Asia spreads dengue, yellow fever, and Chikungunya — what is it called?
Aedes albopictus: Species of mosquito. The insect is called a tiger mosquito as it has stripes, as does a tiger.
This diverse group of photosynthetic organisms ranges from microscopic plankton to seaweeds 50 metres long — yet excludes the land plants entirely. What is it?
Algae: Diverse group of photosynthetic organisms. Algae (AL-jee, UK also AL-ghee; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
Critically endangered with barely two dozen wild individuals estimated in 2007, this big cat subspecies survives along the Russian-Chinese border in the Primorye region — which spotted predator?
Amur leopard: Subspecies of large cat. The Amur leopard (Panthera pardus orientalis) is a leopard subspecies native to the Primorye region of southeastern Russia and northern China.
This external body opening at the end of the digestive tract, positioned opposite the mouth, lets gas and solid waste pass out after digestion?
Anus: Digestive tract waste expulsion opening. Passage of feces through the anus is typically controlled by muscular sphincters, and failure to stop unwanted passages results in fecal incontinence.
Native to Eurasia, this perennial plant is grown as a vegetable crop for its tender young shoots, harvested in the spring — what's this vegetable?
Asparagus: Species of flowering plant in the family Asparagaceae.
A Kenyan economist who met his future wife at the University of Hawaii, this man became the father of a future U.S. president and the subject of that son's 1995 memoir — who is he?
Produced continuously by the liver and stored in the gallbladder, this yellow-green fluid is released into the small intestine to help digest fats — what is it?
Bile: Dark greenish-brown fluid aiding in the digestion of fats.
Named for a Native American people of Oregon and Washington, this tandem-rotor heavy-lift helicopter grew out of Vertol's 1957 Model 107 design — what aircraft is it?
Boeing CH-47 Chinook: American tandem-rotor helicopter introduced in 1962 during the Cold War.
This group of roughly 20,000 non-vascular land plant species — liverworts, hornworts, and mosses — reproduces by spores instead of flowers or seeds. What is it called?
Bryophyte: Terrestrial plants that lack vascular tissue.
This biological family includes wolves, foxes, jackals, and domestic dogs, ranging in size from the 6.6-foot gray wolf down to the tiny fennec fox — what is it called?
Canidae: Family of mammals. Canidae (from Latin, canis, "dog") is a biological family of caniform carnivorans, constituting a clade.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine, this class of molecules includes adrenaline, noradrenaline, and dopamine, and drives the fight-or-flight response when released from the adrenal glands. What are they called?
Caused by a member of the herpesvirus family, this airborne illness usually starts on the chest, back, and face before the itchy little blisters scab over all over the body — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Anafranil, this tricyclic antidepressant treats obsessive-compulsive disorder but also premature ejaculation and the cataplexy that comes with narcolepsy — which drug?
Clomipramine: Antidepressant. It has also been notably used to treat premature ejaculation and the cataplexy associated with narcolepsy.
Once classified among the thrushes, this small Old World flycatcher was later reassigned to the family Muscicapidae — which bird?
Common redstart: Species of bird. The common redstart (Phoenicurus phoenicurus), or often simply redstart, is a small passerine bird in the genus Phoenicurus.
Stalked ones anchored to the seafloor are nicknamed 'sea lilies' while the free-swimming kind are 'feather stars' — what's the class name for these mouth-on-top echinoderms?

Cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years despite not being formally described until 1780, this tree produces the most widely grown fruit in its genus, known by names like Japanese or Chinese persimmon. Which species?
Diospyros kaki: Oriental fruit. Although its first botanical description was not published until 1780, D. kaki cultivation in China dates back more than 2000 years.
Known medically as cerumen, this waxy secretion in the ear canal protects against bacteria, fungi, and water while trapping dust and dead skin — what is it?
Earwax: Waxy substance secreted by the ear.

This discipline systematically applies science and math to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft, with traditional branches in civil, mechanical, electrical, and chemical work — which field?
This small finch native to Europe and Asia is the original species to bear its common English name, and goes by 'plum bird' in Shropshire — what is it?
Eurasian bullfinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian bullfinch or common bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Native to North African deserts from Western Sahara to the Sinai, this diminutive canid uses its oversized ears to shed heat and detect prey burrowing underground — which species is it?
Fennec fox: Species of fox. The fennec fox (Vulpes zerda) is a small fox native to the deserts of North Africa, ranging from Western Sahara and Mauritania to the Sinai Peninsula.
Developed by IBM with a reference manual released in 1956, this programming language became the go-to choice for numerical weather prediction and supercomputer benchmarks — what language is it?
Running from mouth to anus, this passageway includes the esophagus, stomach, and intestines and handles digestion and nutrient absorption — what is it?
Gastrointestinal tract: Organ system within humans and other animals.
Built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, this tripeptide is the most abundant low-mass thiol in most cells and a key antioxidant guarding against free radicals — what is it?
Glutathione: Ubiquitous antioxidant compound in living organisms.

Native to Africa and among the oldest of the chicken-like Galliformes birds, one domesticated species of this family wears a distinctive helmet-shaped casque and has been introduced worldwide — what are they?
Guinea fowl: Family of birds. Guinea fowl or guineafowl are birds of the family Numididae in the order Galliformes.
This localized pooling of blood outside the vessels — often triggered by injury, surgery, or blood-thinning medication — starts out liquid before clotting solid within the tissue. What is it called?
Hematoma: Localized bleeding outside of blood vessels. An ecchymosis is a hematoma of the skin larger than 10 mm.
Ashy-grey with a black head, throat and wings, this corvid was split into its own species in 2002 only to be folded back into its all-black relative by a 2025 reclassification — name the bird?
Hooded crow: Species of bird. The hooded crow (Corvus corone cornix), also colloquially called just hoodie, is a Eurasian bird subspecies of the carrion crow (Corvus corone) in the genus Corvus.

Affecting roughly one in 250 baby boys, this is the second most common birth defect of the male reproductive system, in which a key opening doesn't form in its usual place — what is this condition called?
Hypospadias: Malformation in which the urethral opening is misplaced.
Named after the Greek word for rainbow because its compounds show so many colors, this brittle silvery-white metal is the second-densest element found in nature — what is it?
Iridium: Chemical element with atomic number 77 (Ir)
Built from an umbrella-shaped bell of mesoglea that pulses to swim, this Cnidarian trails stinging tentacles and is the medusa phase of its complex life cycle — what is it?
Native to tropical Southeast Asia, this bumpy-skinned citrus fruit is prized in regional cooking for its intensely fragrant leaves and rind, and its oil is used in perfumery — which fruit?
Kaffir lime: Citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia. Citrus hystrix, called the kaffir lime, Thai lime or makrut lime, (US:, UK:) is a citrus fruit native to tropical Southeast Asia.
Named from Greek words for 'hare' and 'form,' this mammalian order splits into rabbits-and-hares on one branch and pikas on the other, totaling around 110 living species — which order?
Cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and reproduction are its hallmarks — and every instance of it eventually reaches death. What capacity in matter is this?
This French chemist's discoveries in fermentation and vaccination gave us a heat-treatment process that now bears his name and rabies and anthrax vaccines — who was he?
Louis Pasteur: French chemist, pharmacist and microbiologist (1822–1895)
In larger organizations it stacks into a pyramid, with a board and CEO at the top setting strategy — the broad practice of administering a business or government. What is it?
Management: Coordinating the efforts of persons.
Diagnosis, prognosis, prevention, treatment and palliation of injury and disease — drawing on biomedical science, genetics and technology — define this science and practice. What is it?

Medicine: Diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of illness. Medicine encompasses a variety of health care practices which evolved to maintain and restore health through the prevention and treatment of illness and infection.
This theoretical physicist and science communicator bridged science and science fiction well enough to win a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for Arthur C. Clarke — who is he?
Michio Kaku: American theoretical physicist, futurist and author.

Thought to enjoy 'hybrid vigor' and a reduced risk of inbreeding-linked health problems, this catch-all term covers roughly 150 million dogs worldwide that don't belong to any officially recognized breed — what's it called?
This arthropod subphylum includes millipedes and centipedes, and one of its earliest fossils preserves the first known evidence of animals breathing air on land. What's the group called?
Myriapoda: Subphylum of arthropods. The group contains about 13,000 species, all of them terrestrial.
This Serbian-American engineer designed the modern alternating current electricity supply system—the backbone of today's power grid. Who?
Nikola Tesla: Serbian-American engineer and inventor (1856–1943)

Distinct from an unrelated American family with a similar name, these small seed-eating birds include house- and tree-dwelling species that nest on buildings in huge city numbers — which bird family is this?
Old World sparrow: Family of songbirds. Old World sparrows are groups of small passerine birds forming the family Passeridae.
Nicknamed 'forever chemicals' for their long environmental lifetimes, this class of synthetic compounds has been used in everything from Teflon to firefighting foam since 1938 — what's it called?
PFAS: Class of perfluorinated chemical compounds.
Whose name comes from Greek words for 'congealed' and 'curdled' — this plant-cell-wall polymer is extracted from citrus as a powder that makes jams and jellies set?
Pectin: Structural carbohydrate in the cell walls of land plants and some algae.

Nicknamed 'banana spiders' and 'armed spiders' for their aggressive posture, this genus found mainly in northern South America is better known by a name describing its roaming habits — what genus is this?

Nearly odorless with a faintly sweet taste, this diol is approved as a food additive under E-number E1520 and serves as a solvent vehicle in many medications — which compound?
Propylene glycol: Chemical compound. Propylene glycol (IUPAC name: propane-1,2-diol) is a viscous, colorless liquid.
Also known as the holly oak, this large evergreen tree native to the Mediterranean produces acorns that mature within a single summer — which species is it?
Quercus ilex: Oak tree species native to the Mediterranean.

Almost exclusively affecting girls and emerging by 18 months of age, this genetic disorder — usually caused by a mutation in the MECP2 gene — brings language and coordination loss along with repetitive hand movements. What is it?
Rett syndrome: Genetic brain disorder. Rett syndrome (RTT) is a genetic disorder that typically becomes apparent after 6–18 months of age and almost exclusively in girls.

Also called 'German measles,' this vaccine-preventable viral infection is usually mild but can cause severe birth defects — including cataracts and deafness — if a mother catches it early in pregnancy. What disease is it?
Rubella: Human viral disease. Rubella, also known as German measles or three-day measles, is a vaccine-preventable infection caused by the rubella virus.
Named after the Latin word for a small shovel, this flat triangular bone connects the upper arm bone to the collarbone and forms the back of the shoulder girdle — what is it?
Scapula: Bone that connects the humerus and clavicle.
An adult female of this ruminant is a ewe, a castrated male a wether, and a young one a lamb — and with about 1.2 billion of them, they're easily the most common of their kind. What animal?
Sheep: Domesticated ruminant bred for meat, wool, and milk.
Nicknamed a 'truth serum' in popular culture despite dubious real-world reliability, this fast-acting barbiturate anesthetic is marketed under the brand name Pentothal — which drug?
Sodium thiopental: Barbiturate general anesthetic. It is the thiobarbiturate analog of pentobarbital, and an analog of thiobarbital.
This English clergyman was the first person ever to measure blood pressure, and on the side he invented a ventilator and even wrote a tract against drinking — who was he?
Stephen Hales: English clergyman and scientist (1677–1761)
Native to tropical Africa, this berry's glycoprotein — called miraculin — tricks your tongue into tasting sour foods like lemons and limes as sweet; what is this plant commonly nicknamed?
Synsepalum dulcificum: Plant from West Africa with a taste-modifying berry.
Named from Greek for 'four teeth,' this family includes the pufferfish, blowfish, and toadfish — many of them among the most poisonous vertebrates alive. What is this family called?
Tetraodontidae: Family of pufferfish. Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.

Sold under the brand name Zanaflex, this alpha-2 adrenergic agonist treats muscle spasticity from spinal cord injuries and multiple sclerosis, and racked up over 8 million US prescriptions in 2023 — what is it?
Nicknamed 'Crusty' by NATO, this twin-engined Soviet airliner featured a glazed nose and could operate from unpaved airfields — which aircraft is it?
Described from Mongolian fossils in 1924 and smaller than relatives like Deinonychus, which feathered, sickle-clawed dinosaur genus roamed Late Cretaceous Asia?
Velociraptor: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur. The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924.
A slow-moving filter-feeder and the largest known fish alive — the biggest reliably recorded stretched nearly 19 metres — this is the only living member of its family. What is it?
Whale shark: Largest living species of fish. The whale shark (Rhincodon typus) is a slow-moving, filter-feeding carpet shark and the largest known extant fish species.

Distinguished by a fatty hump on its shoulders and a large dewlap, this heat-tolerant type of domestic cattle originated in South Asia and holds religious significance in parts of the world — what is it?
Zebu: South Asian domestic cattle. The zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.
